claims.statement: Store (src/haap_directory/store.py) is the directory's only SQL owner: all persistence SQL lives in that one file, and every state change in the system funnels through a Store method that persists it and appends the matching L5 audit entry.

The Store concurrency model is a single sqlite3 connection with check_same_thread=False, WAL journal mode, isolation_level=None (manual transaction control), and PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON plus busy_timeout=5000; every read and write is guarded by one threading.RLock held on the Store instance, and there are no connection pools and no async database access.

All writes go through the _write() context manager, which acquires the RLock, executes BEGIN IMMEDIATE, yields a cursor, then COMMITs or — on any exception — ROLLBACKs and re-raises; reads are plain autocommit SELECTs under the same RLock and never open a transaction.

The audit-equals-mutation invariant: every Store method that changes directory state appends exactly one audit entry via _append_audit inside the same write transaction in which the mutation occurs, so 'audit rows == mutating ops' holds by construction and there is no window where state moved without a log line.

One request may legitimately produce several chain entries when it performs several distinct state changes in one transaction: insert_challenge appends challenge.evicted when it evicts the oldest pending challenge and then appends register.challenge_issued; prune_expired appends one agent.expired entry per agent row it transitions.

Two Store writers intentionally do not extend the audit chain: insert_checkpoint persists a directory signature over the chain head into checkpoints (an external attestation, by design), and mark_challenge_used mutates a challenge row without an audit append yet has no callers anywhere in the tree — the real paths consume challenges inside complete_registration and confirm_domain_verification, which do audit.

_append_audit derives seq and prev_hash by reading the audit head through the caller's open transaction under the write lock (seq 0 and prev_hash '0'*64 when the log is empty, otherwise head seq + 1 and the head entry_hash), builds the canonical entry, inserts it into audit_log, and maintains the meta chain_head_seq row with INSERT OR REPLACE.

Genesis: Store._ensure_genesis runs at construction and, when audit_log is empty, appends the seq-0 entry with event chain.genesis, actor 'directory', result 'ok', detail {schema_version} and prev_hash '0'*64 inside its own write transaction.

Normative chain math in audit.py: entry[n] = {seq, ts, event, fingerprint, actor, result, detail_hash, prev_hash}, entry_hash[n] = sha256(canonical_json(entry[n])), genesis prev_hash is '0' repeated 64 times, and verify_chain recomputes every entry_hash from the eight canonical fields and checks prev_hash linkage, so any modification, deletion, or reordering changes descendant hashes and the head.

detail_hash is the sha256 hex of the canonical JSON of a detail object ({} when None), so sensitive detail bodies never enter the public chain — only their hash does; the test suite asserts every stored detail_hash is 64 hex characters and that per-agent audit responses expose detail_hash but never a detail body.

Canonical JSON (canonical.py) is json.dumps with sort_keys, compact separators and ensure_ascii=False encoded as UTF-8, deliberately vendored so the directory has no hard import dependency on the haap client package while remaining byte-for-byte identical to the client's serializer — any deviation would break hashes and signatures.

All time — expiry arithmetic, registration timestamps, and audit entry ts — is read through an injected Clock callable (Store(db_path, clock=system_clock), self.now()); nothing in store.py calls time.time() directly, and tests inject a MutableClock to exercise TTL expiry and checkpoint cadence deterministically.

Timestamps are stored twice — fixed-width RFC 3339 UTC text (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, integer-second truncation making strings signature-stable and lexicographically ordered) for the wire, and integer epoch columns for comparisons and indexed expiry queries; to_rfc3339/from_rfc3339 in timeutil.py are the only formatters.

The SQLite schema is defined by the _SCHEMA constant (SCHEMA_VERSION '1') and applied idempotently at startup via executescript (which auto-commits in its own transaction and must not be nested in a manual BEGIN) plus an INSERT OR IGNORE meta.schema_version row; the nine tables are meta, agents, challenges, domain_verifications, vouches, reports, audit_log, checkpoints, and appeals, and schema evolution in v1 is additive.

Expiry is TTL-driven and clock-based: 'live' means status='listed', is_history=0 and expires_epoch >= int(now); prune_expired transitions listed entries past their TTL to status='expired' with is_history=1 and one audited agent.expired entry per row in a single transaction, is idempotent, and runs on service startup, via haap-dird --prune, and lazily before live_agents() and count_live() reads.

Registration refresh and heartbeat renewal semantics: _upsert_agent_cur preserves registered_at/registered_epoch on a live re-registration (audited register.updated) and treats an expired or absent fingerprint as a fresh insert (audited register.completed); heartbeat renews last_heartbeat and expires fields only while the row is still live, emitting heartbeat.ok or heartbeat.legacy_unsigned.

Single-use challenge semantics are enforced inside the write transaction: complete_registration and confirm_domain_verification re-check the challenges.used flag after BEGIN IMMEDIATE and raise CHALLENGE_USED / VERIFICATION_USED on a replay, so a replayed completion loses the race under the write lock.

Expired challenges, domain verifications and vouches are not deleted or transitioned — readers filter on expires_epoch at query time (active_domain_verifications, inbound_vouches active_only, pending-challenge counts); only agents get the audited expired transition, and challenges may be evicted (challenge.evicted) when a new endpoint challenge exceeds the pending cap.

Checkpoint persistence: the checkpoints table is keyed by seq equal to the audit head seq at signing time and written with INSERT OR REPLACE (at most one checkpoint per head seq); AuditService signs the canonical JSON of {seq, entry_hash, ts} with the directory Ed25519 key, maybe_checkpoint enforces checkpoint_interval_s (3600 s default), a background thread in DirectoryHTTPServer signs on that cadence, and a final checkpoint is written on server shutdown before the store closes.

Audit read paths: audit_head returns {seq, ts, entry_hash} of the last row; audit_entries pages the log in ascending seq order with the limit clamped to 1000 so /v1/audit/log serves contiguous ranges with a consistent head; audit_entries_for_fingerprint returns the redacted projection (seq, ts, event, fingerprint, actor, result, detail_hash) for the per-agent audit view.

Failure semantics are atomic in both directions: every mutator runs inside _write, so any exception — a DirectoryError such as CHALLENGE_NOT_FOUND, CHALLENGE_USED, VOUCH_LIMIT_REACHED, VOUCH_EXISTS, REPORT_EXISTS, or an internal error — rolls back both the state mutation and its audit line, leaving no partial state; race-sensitive guards are therefore re-checked under the write lock inside the transaction.

The audit event taxonomy emitted by Store mutators is stable and caller-supplied where multiple services share one mutator: register.challenge_issued, register.completed, register.updated, heartbeat.ok, heartbeat.legacy_unsigned, agent.expired, domain.verify_requested, domain.verified, vouch.created, vouch.revoked, report.recorded, appeal.submitted, chain.genesis and challenge.evicted from store.py, plus moderator.suspend, moderator.takedown, report.auto_suspend and moderator.unsuspend passed into suspend_agent/unsuspend_agent by the moderation and reputation services.

Schema relationships between domain tables (audit_log.fingerprint, vouches.voucher_fingerprint, reports.target_fingerprint, etc.) are by-value references, not enforced foreign keys — PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is set but no FK constraints are declared, so Store methods perform their own referential and ownership checks (e.g. SIGNATURE_MISMATCH on vouch revocation by a non-voucher, AGENT_NOT_FOUND on suspend) inside their transactions.
